🧠 Crypto News Brief: Binance's record $6.3B hack still dominates: Washington weighs in, investigators point at North Korea and ETF money heads for the exits, while Bitcoin clings to $77K in a fearful market. 🏛️ Trump Says His Administration Is Looking Into the Binance Hack Speaking at a Friday press conference, President Trump said officials are reviewing the $6.3 billion Binance breach, noting the exchange has promised to make customers whole. The incident is fueling fresh calls for federal crypto legislation, with Sen. Lummis arguing the stalled Clarity Act would have given firms legal cover to freeze suspicious transfers quickly. Read full story 🔐 Binance Moves to Restore Confidence as $3B Is Frozen Binance pledged to cover all losses from company funds and plans to reopen withdrawals in phases within days, with a proof-of-reserves snapshot due by Monday. About $3 billion of the stolen assets has been located and frozen; Tether locked nearly $1.57 billion in USDT, Circle more than $800 million in USDC, and the U.S. Secret Service says it is working with Circle to trace and recover funds. More details 🇰🇵 Investigators Tie the $6.3B Heist to North Korea's TraderTraitor TRM Labs attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, the Lazarus-linked North Korean unit behind the 2025 Bybit theft, and Chainalysis CEO Jonathan Levin reached the same view. TRM says roughly $6.36 billion left Binance wallets across ten blockchains, mostly within about 20 minutes. Binance itself has not named a culprit. Read more ⚖️ CFTC Chair Selig: Hack Proves Offshore Exchanges Need U.S. Rules CFTC Chairman Michael Selig told CNBC the Binance breach validates the agency's October proposals, which would offer offshore venues a voluntary federal registration path with U.S.-grade cybersecurity standards. He added that blockchain transparency gives investigators a good chance of tracing the stolen funds. 81716.subject: Weekly Recap: Binance Hack Hits $6.3 Billion
81716.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

**Binance** set the week. On Thursday, an attacker drained its hot wallets of about $6.3 billion by the exchange's estimate. On Friday, Binance said it had reserved $6.34 billion to cover users and aims to restart withdrawals by Sunday. **Aave** raised borrowing limits on Wednesday, froze its markets on Thursday and reopened them on Friday with tighter rules.

Elsewhere, **DTCC** switched on tokenization, and **Robinhood** listed tokens for companies that had objected to OKXICE. Keystone and Trezor warned their own hardware-wallet buyers, and Utah charged Kalshi's founders. **Stellar** tested a fee-free chain during its Meridian conference, where we went live on Thursday.

Enjoy!

———————————————————————————

———————————————————————————

##### WATCH

## Kaiko's $110M Raise, a Nation Onchain, Stablecoins in 190 Countries & More: On the Floor at Stellar's Meridian

We went live from the floor at Stellar's Meridian on Thursday, covering Kaiko's $110 million raise, a nation moving onchain and stablecoins in 190 countries. [Watch the replay on X](https://x.com/DefiantNews/status/2115888802137059518).

———————————————————————————

# Top Stories This Week

## Binance Lost About $6.3 Billion in a Hot-Wallet Hack

On Thursday afternoon, an [EIP-7702 delegation](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/binance-labeled-wallet-swept-minutes-after-eip-7702-delegation) gave an outside address control of a Binance hot wallet, and [billions left three Ethereum wallets](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-wallet-outflows-widen-to-three-accounts-in-suspected-hack). Binance paused withdrawals. Tether blacklisted the receiving address 37 minutes after the first transfer and [froze more than 1.567 billion USDT](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/tether-freezes-971-million-usdt-in-wallet-linked-to-suspected-binance-drain), and Circle froze more than 800 million USDC. On Friday, Binance put the impact at about $6.3 billion and [reserved $6.34 billion](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-it-has-reserved-over-6-34-billion-to-cover-hack-losses) of company funds to cover it. Co-CEO Richard Teng targeted a withdrawal restart [before Sunday](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-s-teng-targets-sunday-withdrawal-restart-after-hack) and a reserve report [by Monday](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-s-teng-sets-monday-reserve-report-deadline-as-withdrawals-stay-paused). Chainalysis [linked the attack to North Korea](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainalysis-links-6-4-billion-binance-hack-to-north-korea) and said the attacker [swapped $325 million of stablecoins into ether](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainalysis-says-binance-hacker-swapped-325-million-to-evade-freezes) to get ahead of freezes. Our EIP-7702 explainer was the most-read story of the week, and our [timeline and FAQ](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-security-incident-withdrawal-status-timeline-and-faqs) tracks the withdrawal status.
